# Prey (2017) internals - notes from three Chairloader DLL mods

Written for the PreyVR / motion-controls effort by Vittorio "Vee" Romeo, September 2026. Everything below was
learned while building three DLL mods on the Chairloader framework and is offered freely (the mods are MIT):

* **Viewmodel Tweaks & Ironsights** - <https://github.com/vittorioromeo/Vee.ViewmodelTweaks> - moves the
  weapon and first-person arms to arbitrary camera-relative poses (hip offsets, ironsights lock, sway, recoil,
  FOV control). The most VR-relevant one: it is, in effect, "place the weapon and hands where I say, every frame".
* **Mediumcore Death** - <https://github.com/vittorioromeo/Vee.Mediumcore> - death rework, inventory, saves,
  traumas, signals.
* **Simulation Rollback** - <https://github.com/vittorioromeo/Vee.SimulationRollback> - save/load by name,
  voice lines, subtitles, Bink videos, post effects, HUD drawing.

Each repository has a `DEVNOTES.md` with more detail and the source is small enough to read in one sitting.
This document collects the parts most likely to matter for a VR conversion and the traps that cost us crashes.
It is written to be pasted into an LLM's context as well as read by a human; sections are self-contained.

**Build targeted:** Steam Prey 1.0.1.0 as patched by Chairloader to the EGS 2021-08-18 `PreyDll.dll` (the
only build Chairloader supports; Chairloader replaces the Steam DLL with it). All RVAs are into that
`PreyDll.dll` unless stated. `PreyDll.dll` is monolithic: CryEngine (system, renderer, entity system, action,
audio ATL) *and* the game code are one module; `Prey.exe` is a thin launcher.

---

## 1. Tooling and workflow

### Chairloader
* <https://github.com/thelivingdiamond/Chairloader> - mod loader with a PDB-derived SDK (`Common/Prey/**/*.h`),
  hooking (`PreyFunction<Sig>(rva).MakeHook()` + `SetHookFunc`, `InvokeOrig`), ImGui overlay (F1), cvar
  persistence (`REGISTER_CVAR2` with `VF_DUMPTOCHAIR` -> `Mods/config/Chairloader_CVars.xml`), a hot-reload
  cycle, and `ChairManager/PreyFiles/` = the game's paks extracted (XML data, localization, levels). Mods are
  `Prey/Mods/<Name>/{ModInfo.xml, <Name>.dll}`.
* The SDK headers are generated from Arkane's PDB, so class layouts, member offsets and static/member function
  RVAs are almost always right. Interface *vtable orders* copied from stock CryEngine are **not** always right
  (section 3).
* Mod lifecycle hooks and where they run: `UpdateBeforeSystem` from a `CGame::Update` hook *before* the
  original; `MainUpdate` from a `CSystem::Update` hook *after* the original; `LateUpdate` from
  `CCryAction::PostUpdate` (HUD drawing goes here); `Draw` inside the ImGui frame.
* Unregister your cvars in `ShutdownSystem` (`IConsole::UnregisterVariable(name, true)` for your prefix); the
  console keeps raw pointers to name/help/storage that vanish with your DLL and touches them at engine shutdown
  (crash on exit otherwise).
* The F1 GUI shows the hardware cursor, so `CHardwareMouse::m_iReferenceCounter > 0` also fires for it; check
  `gCL->gui->IsEnabled()` before treating a visible cursor as "game menu open".

### Reverse engineering
* Ghidra headless is fast enough to decompile single functions on demand: `analyzeHeadless <proj> <name>
  -process PreyDll.dll -noanalysis -postScript <script>` with a script that takes `0x18XXXXXXX Name` lines,
  `disassemble()` + `CreateFunctionCmd`, then `DecompInterface`. The SDK's `PreyFunction` RVAs are your entry
  points; `0x180000000` is the preferred image base. No RTTI names survive in the binary, so find vtables via
  the constructor's `lea rax, [rip+vtable]`.
* capstone + pefile for quick disassembly around an address and for dumping vtables / strings.
* Crash triage: `Game.log` prints the call stack as raw addresses. Map them to modules with the module list of
  the minidump (`error.dmp` in the Prey root, MINIDUMP module stream), symbolize your own frames with
  `llvm-symbolizer --obj=<your.dll> --relative-address <rva>` against your PDB, and disassemble the game's
  frame around the *return address* (the instruction before it is the call).
* Cross-compiling on Linux works: clang-cl + lld-link against copied MSVC/Windows SDK headers (the official
  route is VS2022 + CMake + vcpkg). clang-cl matched the MSVC ABI in every case we checked, with one
  miscompile (section 3, `Draw2dLabel`).
* Struct offsets in the SDK can be checked at compile time: `template<int N> struct Probe; Probe<offsetof(T, m)> p;`
  with `-fsyntax-only` prints the value in the error.

### A patch worth knowing about
* Random `EXCEPTION_STACK_OVERFLOW` in `JobSystem_Worker` threads in `CParticleContainer::UpdateParticles`
  (a large `alloca` for particle sorting). Worker threads inherit `Prey.exe`'s default stack size
  (`SizeOfStackReserve` = 1 MB). Patching the PE header to 8 MB (and zeroing the checksum) removed the crashes.
  A VR build that pushes more particles per frame may hit this sooner.

---

## 2. Calling-convention and layout traps (each cost a crash)

1. **Struct returns > 8 bytes** (`QuatT`, `std::vector`, `std::pair`, ...): for member functions the hidden
   return pointer comes **after** `this`: `R* fn(T* _this, R* _ret, args...)`. Several SDK headers declare
   these as returning the struct directly (`ArkItemSystem::GiveArchetype`, `IEntity::CreateProxy`, ...);
   declare your own `PreyFunction` with the real layout.
2. **8-byte structs with a user-declared constructor** (`ArkBinkPlayerHandle`) are *returned* through a hidden
   pointer (MSVC rule: no user-defined ctor/dtor/copy for register return) but *passed* by value in a register
   (they are still trivially copyable). Handle both when calling through raw function pointers.
3. **`PreyFunction` objects are rebased at DLL init.** A function-local `static PreyFunction` is constructed
   too late and calls the raw RVA. Keep them at file/class scope.
4. **The SDK's `physinterface.h` is stock CryEngine; Prey's physics structs are bigger.** `pe_status_living`
   is 152 bytes in Prey (an extra `Vec3` after `velGround`, `groundSurfaceIdx` at +0x64 not +0x58) vs. 136 in
   the header. `GetStatus()` into a header-sized stack local silently overwrote the caller's saved `xmm6`
   (our frame `dt`), producing wrong smoothing with no crash. Rule: every struct *the game fills in*
   (`pe_status_*`, `ray_hit`, `SLocalizedInfoGame`, ...) gets Prey's layout when known and a generous pad after
   it regardless.
5. **Prey added parameters to some engine functions.** `ILocalizationManager::LocalizeString(const char*,
   wstring&, bool bEnglish, void** pOutHolder)` has a 5th out-pointer the header lacks; leaving it to the stack
   garbage made the game write through it. `IEntityAudioProxy::ExecuteTrigger(trigger, ELipSyncMethod,
   proxyId, callbacks)` likewise has the CE 3.8 lip-sync parameter.
6. **`IRenderAuxGeom::Draw2dLabel(..., fmt, ...)`** (inline variadic wrapper in the header) was miscompiled by
   clang-cl at one call site: the `va_list` pointed at the argument's bytes instead of its slot. Call
   `RenderText(Vec3, SDrawTextInfo&, "%s", va_list)` yourself with `const char* p = text; (va_list)&p`.

---

## 3. SDK vtable order vs. the binary

Verified by decompiling the game's own callers. Where the header is wrong, call by byte offset
(`((R(**)(void*, Args...))*(void**)obj)[off/8](obj, args...)`).

| Interface | Header | Real slots (byte offsets) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IGameFramework` | two virtuals short in places | `+0x120` GetISubtitleManager, `+0x1D8` GetArkSaveLoadSystem (then `+0x08` GetCampaignSlot), `+0x298` SaveGame(path, quick, immediate, reason, ignoreDelay, checkpoint), `+0x2A0` LoadGame(path, quick, ignoreDelay). `IsGameStarted/IsGamePaused/GetLevelName` via the header are fine. |
| `IEntity` | two spurious virtuals at the front (`SetLocalSeg/IsLocalSeg`); `GetId` is really slot 1 | `+0x08` GetId, `+0xE8` GetWorldTM, `+0x210` CreateProxy(type) -> shared_ptr via hidden ptr. Prefer `CEntity::FGetProxy` (0x904D50) / `FCreateProxy` (0x903540) statics from `CryEntitySystem/Entity.h` (that class header is PDB-derived and correct). |
| `ILocalizationManager` | two slots low | `+0x80` LocalizeString(const char*, wstring&, bool, void**), `+0x98` GetLocalizedInfoByKey(key, SLocalizedInfoGame&). `ISystem::GetLocalizationManager` (`+0x4A0`) via header is fine. |
| `IRenderer` | two slots high at the tail | `+0x898` GetIArkBinkManager(). Everything we used before that (`GetWidth/GetHeight`, `SetState`, `Draw2dImage`, `GetWhiteTextureId`, `GetIRenderAuxGeom`) matched. |
| `IEntityAudioProxy` (`CEntityAudioProxy` vtable @ 0x181d28e08) | order differs | `+0xA8` CreateAuxAudioProxy(bool) -> id, `+0xB0` RemoveAuxAudioProxy(id), `+0xD8` ExecuteTrigger(trigger, lipSync, proxyId, const SAudioCallBackInfos&), `+0xF8` SetEnvironmentAmount(env, amount, proxyId), `+0x120` SetObstructionCalcType(type, proxyId). Entity audio proxies wrap `IAudioProxy` objects from `IAudioSystem::GetFreeAudioProxy()` (`+0x98`). |
| `IAudioSystem`, `ISystem`, `IArkBinkManager`, `IArkDialogAudioManager`, `IRenderAuxGeom`, `ISubtitleManager`, `IAnimationOperatorQueue`, `ISkeletonPose`, `IDefaultSkeleton`, `IAttachmentManager`, `IAttachment` | match | (slots we relied on are listed where used below) |

---

## 4. Camera, first-person arms and the weapon - the pipeline VR has to bend

Prey kept Crysis 3's first-person setup. The order of operations per frame matters for anything that wants to
put the camera or the weapon somewhere else:

1. `ArkPlayerCamera::PrePhysicsUpdate` updates `m_rotation` (view `Ang3`: pitch = x, yaw = z) from input and
   smooths `m_leanAmount` (10/s).
2. The first-person *arms character* is animated (mannequin). `CProceduralWeaponAnimationContext::Update`
   (0x17D4D50) calls `CProceduralWeaponAnimation::Update(dt)` (0x17D31E0), which blends the weapon's authored
   pose offsets, look/strafe sway, recoil, bumps and zoom into two view-space `QuatT`s: `m_rightOffset`
   (`this+0x2D8`, weapon hand) and `m_leftOffset` (`this+0x2F4`, support hand). The context rotates them into
   the aim frame (`Quat::CreateRotationVDir(aimDir)`) and pushes them **additively** onto the hand IK joints
   through an `IAnimationOperatorQueue` pose modifier (joint index at `ctx+0x18`; queue slots 8/9 = push
   position / orientation with `eOp_Override=?`/`eOp_Additive=3`). Some mannequin fragments (jump/land)
   have no weapon procedural clip; the context early-outs on `m_instanceCount < 1` and nothing is applied
   (the weapon snaps back) - we hook that function and force the count to 1.
3. **The camera is built *from* the skeleton, not the other way round.** `ArkPlayerCamera::UpdateView`
   (0x145ED50) -> `GetDesiredPositionAndRotation` (0x145C530) reads the `#camera` attachment of the arms
   character (`IAttachmentManager::GetInterfaceByName` = vtable `+0x38`, `IAttachment::GetAttModelRelative` =
   `+0x68`), rotates it by the entity rotation, and combines view angles with lean roll
   (`m_leanAngle * m_leanAmount`). The position is returned *relative to the entity* because the arms render
   in camera space (`ENTITY_SLOT_RENDER_NEAREST`; `CView::Update` adds the entity position). Nothing touches the
   skeleton between this call and rendering -> **post-hooking `GetDesiredPositionAndRotation` is the last
   moment to override camera and/or weapon transforms consistently.** For VR: this is where an HMD pose can
   replace the game's camera while the arms still follow.
4. **The weapon is not rendered from its own entity.** `CArkWeapon::AttachToHand` binds the weapon's character
   as a skeleton attachment (`CSKELAttachment`) of the arms and clears the weapon entity's render flag; it is
   drawn at `armsWorldMatrix * CAttachmentBONE::m_AttModelRelative` (a `QuatT` at `attachment+0x130`;
   `GetAttModelRelative()` returns a reference to it, so it can be written directly).
   `CArkWeapon::m_pAttachment` is at `+0x2B0`. Muzzle flash / projectile origin are attached to the weapon
   bone, so moving the weapon moves the shot origin too.
5. Hand joints follow via the final absolute pose buffer `ISkeletonPose::GetAbsJointByID` (slot 24) returns by
   reference - the skinning reads it at render time, so you can rigidly move the weapon-hand subtree (and the
   support hand when it is near the weapon) after step 3. Hierarchy: `IDefaultSkeleton` `GetJointCount` slot 1,
   `GetJointParentIDByID` 2, `GetJointNameByID` 6, `GetJointIDByName` 7; the weapon hangs off `r_handProp_jnt`
   (child of the right hand joint).

What the Ironsights mod does with this (directly reusable for motion controls, replacing "aim pose" with
"controller pose"):
* **Skeleton side**, after the context pushed its operators: push `eOp_Additive` position/orientation for the
  weapon-hand IK joint so the hand lands on `camera(model) * pose * (weapon relative to IK joint)^-1`. Uses the
  previous frame's camera + this frame's mouse delta (the camera is not final yet). Using `eOp_Override`
  instead kills the authored fire/reload hand animation; additive keeps it, and the game's own frame-old
  additive is subtracted back out to recover the pure animation (used to extract the recoil kick).
* **Render side**, in the `GetDesiredPositionAndRotation` post-hook: write `m_AttModelRelative =
  camera(model) * pose` and move the hand joint subtree by the same rigid delta. Deterministic, no filtering
  -> no jitter. Everything read from the game is checked for finiteness / near-unit quaternions; accumulated
  state is reset on bad numbers (`Ang3(Quat)` in CryMath uses an unclamped `asin`).
* Per-weapon poses keyed by `IEntityClass::GetName()` of the equipped `CArkWeapon`.

Other pieces around the pipeline:
* **Near FOV.** The arms/weapon render in the "nearest" pass with their own FOV in `r_DrawNearFoV`
  (`EFQ_Set/GetDrawNearFov`). `ArkPlayerZoomManager::Reset()` / `SetNearFOVUnlocked()` hard-code 55 deg and
  `ArkPlayerZoomManager::Update()` rescales it while zooming - a `game.cfg` value never sticks; re-apply per
  frame after the game's update. Camera FOV: `ArkPlayerZoomManager::SetDesiredHFOV(hfov, time, false, high)` /
  `ClearDesiredHFOV`; `cl_hfov` is the base.
* **Player state** useful for gating: `ArkPlayer::GetInstancePtr()`, `m_stance` (`STANCE_SNEAK` = crouch),
  `m_bInTrackview` (scripted sequence / cutscene), `ArkPlayerMovementFSM::IsSprinting()` (0x1570580) /
  `IsInZeroG()` (0x1570370), `ArkPlayer::IsInCombat()` (0x15514A0: list of NPCs fighting the player is
  non-empty), `ArkPlayerAwarenessComponent::m_awarenessStates` (`VectorMap<EntityId, {m_level:
  EArkAttentionLevel unknown/noticed/curious/interested/known}>`), velocity from `pe_status_living::vel` (see
  the size trap).
* **Weapon state** (`CArkWeapon`): `m_bIsReadyToAttack` @ `+0x48B` (cleared for select, reload *and* every
  shot), `m_bIsReloading` @ `+0x48C`, `m_bIsUnequipping` @ `+0x48D`, `m_condition` (0..100),
  `CArkWeapon::FireWeapon` (0x16659B0) is the shot event for every weapon. `ArkPlayerWeaponComponent`:
  `m_equippedWeaponId`, `m_toBeEquippedWeaponId` @ `+0x64`, `m_bIsUnequipping` @ `+0x78`. The draw animation
  has a window where the arms are not yet valid for overrides - we gate on ready + a minimum delay after the
  equipped id changed (0.75 s worked for all weapons).
* Procedural offsets you may want to keep or kill: `CRecoilOffset/CBumpOffset/CLookOffset/CStrafeOffset::Compute`
  can be hooked to capture (and scale) what the game adds.
* Time: `gEnv->pTimer->GetRealFrameTime()` for real time; `GetAsyncTime()` as int64 ticks for a clock that does
  not freeze in menus. `ITimer::GetFrameTime()` is scaled/paused game time.

---

## 5. Input, reticle, in-world screens

* Mod key bindings: an `IInputEventListener` registered with `gEnv->pInput` receives raw events; events are
  not delivered while a cursor is on screen, which is the behaviour you want for gameplay binds.
* Action maps: the UI enables/disables the `"UIInput"` action map through `CUIManager` (the `Ark:BinkMovie`
  flow node calls `GetActionMap("UIInput")` then `Enable(true)` after a movie).
* Reticle: `hud_reticleSetting` (`SCVars+0x930`; 0 off, 1 default, 2 dot) is what the options menu writes;
  its only readers are 4 sites in `CArkUIHUD`; at 0 the HUD gets `reticleDisplay("none")` *and*
  `interactIconDisplay("none")`.
* **In-world screens use the HUD reticle as the cursor**: `ArkExaminationMode::UpdateReticlePos` (0x157EBA0)
  moves `m_reticlePos` (`+0x60`) and sends `reticlePosition` to the HUD. State:
  `ArkPlayer::m_examinationMode.m_examinationState != inactive` with `m_examinationType == worldUI`. For a VR
  laser pointer this is the hook: feed your own screen position into that path.
* The HUD is Scaleform Flash (`IUIElement`, events like `reticlePosition`, `subtitleUpdate`,
  `audioLogUpdate`), reached through `CGame::m_pUIManager` (`CUIManager::GetUIEventSystem("<TypeName>")`
  returns the game-side event system object, e.g. `"ArkSubtitleHandler"`).

---

## 6. Rendering-side helpers we used

* Full-screen quad / fades: `IRenderer::SetState(GS_BLSRC_SRCALPHA | GS_BLDST_ONEMINUSSRCALPHA |
  GS_NODEPTHTEST)` then `Draw2dImage(x, y, w, h, GetWhiteTextureId(), 0,0,1,1, 0, r,g,b,a, 1)`, coordinates in
  an 800x600 virtual space, from `LateUpdate`.
* 2D text: `IRenderAuxGeom::RenderText` (see trap 6); `SDrawTextInfo.flags = eDrawText_2D |
  eDrawText_800x600 [| eDrawText_Center]` puts positions in the same virtual space; size ~12 virtual px per unit.
  Chairloader replaces the engine's aux geom (`CAuxGeomCB`), all of this goes through it.
* Post-process parameters: `I3DEngine::SetPostEffectParam(name, value, force)` with names from
  `Ark/VisualEffects/ArkPostEffectParams.xml`: `VisualArtifacts_Vsync/VsyncFreq/Interlacing/InterlacingTile/
  Pixelation/Noise/SyncWaveFreq/SyncWavePhase/SyncWaveAmplitude`, `FilterArtifacts_ChromaShift/Grain`,
  `Global_User_Saturation/Contrast/Brightness`, `FilterBlurring_Amount`, `ArkPostAliens_Glitch`,
  `AlienInterference_Amount`. Set every frame while active; reset afterwards. (For VR you will probably want
  to *disable* several of the game's screen-space effects; the same parameter names apply.)
* Named game post effects: `Ark/VisualEffects/ArkPostEffects.xml` (64-bit ids),
  `CGame::m_pArkPostEffectManager->EnableEffect(id)` / `DisableEffect(id, blendOut)`. E.g.
  `Player_EndGameVRTermination` = 14610450286789593543 (gamma-to-black then white-out), `Player_Fatality` =
  12635110349617286617, `Player_NearDeath` = 2428940965280750461.
* Bink movies: `IRenderer::GetIArkBinkManager()` (`+0x898`); `IArkBinkManager::MT_LoadMovie(path, instanceId,
  type 1 Fullscreen/2 Background/3 Texture, flags 1 AutoStart|2 Looping)` [slot 3, handle via hidden pointer],
  `MT_ReleaseMovie` [4], `MT_StartMovie` [5], `MT_StopMovie` [6], `MT_IsMoviePlaying` [8]. Fullscreen movies are
  composited by the renderer over the frame - relevant if you need to intercept them for a stereo view.
  Files in `GameSDK/Videos/*.bk2` (`KB2j` header: frame count @+8, w/h @+20/+24, fps @+28/+32).

---

## 7. Audio: voice lines, dialogue, positioning

* Every dialogue line is an ATL trigger `Play_<voiceId><dialogId>` (16 hex digits each), defined in
  `Libs/GameAudio/GameMode/Campaign/Voice_<voiceId>.xml`; text in `Localization/English_xml.pak:
  voices/Voice_<voiceId>.xml`, names in `Ark/Dialog/VoiceLibrary.xml`. Radio voices' banks are resident, but
  **line media is streamed on demand**: `IArkDialogAudioManager::Load(triggerId, IArkDialogLoadListener&)`
  (manager: `CGame::m_pArkResponseManager->GetAudioManager()`) -> `OnLoad(id, ok)` -> execute; `Unload` later.
  Executing without loading "plays" silence.
* **Voice events are positioned 3D sounds**; executing on the global audio object (no position) is silent.
  Radio calls go through `ArkDialogPlayerTranscribe::SetEntity` (0x13F8A50): aux audio proxy on the player
  entity, audio *environment* `"Transcribe"` (`IAudioSystem::GetAudioEnvironmentID`) at 1.0 = the radio filter,
  occlusion ignored, `ExecuteTrigger(trigger, lipSync=1, auxProxyId, callbacks)`.
* `ArkAudioTrigger::Load(name)` / `Execute(IEntity*)` (Ark/ArkAudioUtil.h) is the simple path for SFX;
  `Execute(nullptr)` pushes an `SAudioRequest{flags, objectId 0, ...}` with data `{vtable,
  eART_AUDIO_OBJECT_REQUEST=3, eAORT_EXECUTE_TRIGGER=0x10, triggerId, float 0, lipSync}` (the SDK lacks
  `SAudioObjectRequestData`). The `IAudioSystem` header vtable matches the binary (`PushRequest` +0x18,
  `GetAudioTriggerID` +0x40, `GetAudioEnvironmentID` +0x68, `GetFreeAudioProxy` +0x98).
* For VR: the listener is the camera; moving the camera to the HMD through the camera path above keeps audio
  consistent. Hand-held weapon sounds are attached to the weapon bone (moves with your override).

---

## 8. Subtitles

The game's path (`ArkDialogSubtitleManager::ShowSubtitlePart`, 0x11B4BF0): text from
`ArkDialogSubtitleManager::GetSubtitle(dialogId, voiceId, SLocalizedInfoGame&)` (0x11B44B0; localization key
`"%llX_%llX"` = dialogId_voiceId, fallback `"%llX"`), formatted `"<font color='#FFDF80'>%ls%ls</font> %ls"`
(speaker, `@ui_SubtitleNameSeperator`, text), shown by `ArkSubtitleHandler::ShowSubtitle(wstring,
bMetaGameMenu)` (0x1632330 -> Flash `subtitleUpdate`) and removed by `HideSubtitle` (0x1631C70). Handler:
`CUIManager::GetUIEventSystem("ArkSubtitleHandler")` (`static_cast` from the returned `IUIGameEventSystem*`,
which is at +8). Bink subtitle timings: `Ark/Dialog/BinkSubtitles/<movie>.xml` (frame numbers).

---

## 9. Player health, death, revive

* Health reaching 0: `ArkPlayerHealthComponent::DoDeath()` (0x155E420) holsters, sets the death movement
  state and camera, arms `m_timeRemainingBeforeDeathMenu`. **`ArkPlayerHealthComponent::Update()`
  (0x155F4A0) is the only place that opens the death menu**; skipping the original while `IsDead()` keeps it
  shut with no side effects (`m_bDeathMenuOpened` says if the game got there first).
* `ArkPlayer::Revive()` (0x1556B80) is the dev "Revive" button: reloads the player model, re-attaches the
  weapon, resets the FSM and health. `ForceKill()` (0x155E530) for testing. Scripted deaths have
  `ArkPlayer::m_bInTrackview` set.
* Health changes: `ArkPlayerHealthComponent::SetHealth` (0x155EFE0); consumable/operator effects arrive as
  signals in `ArkPlayerSignalReceiver::OnReceiveSignal` (0x1575690); psi `CArkPsiComponent::IncrementPoints`
  (0x157FFD0); traumas `ArkPlayerStatusComponent::GetTraumaForStatus(status)` -> `ArkTraumaBase`
  (`IsEnabled`, `Activate(level)`), `ReduceStatus(signalId, amount)` (0x14631A0); suit integrity is the
  `SuitIntegrity` trauma.
* Inventory: items are entities - `ArkInventory::GetItemIDs()`, `ArkItemSystem::GetItem(id)`,
  `CArkItem::Drop(count, const Vec3*)` (0x10B0D40), `RemoveFromInventory()`, `IArkItem::ResetCount(n)`,
  `CArkItem::InitializeCount` (0x10B3600) for spawn counts, `ArkFabricator::SpawnItem` (0x1166DE0),
  `ArkItemSystem::GiveArchetype` (returns `std::vector` - see trap 1).
* Level entrances are `SpawnPoint` entities (`Properties.destinationName = "From_<Level>"`);
  `ArkGame::OnLevelTransitionFinished()` (0x116F1A0) fires after a transition placed the player;
  `ArkGame::OnLevelToLevelTransition` (0x116F190) at its start.

---

## 10. Saving and loading

* `ArkGame::SaveToSlot(const char* name, bool immediate)` (0x116FE80, member, bool) is what QuickSave /
  ManualSave / IronmanSave end in: `IGameFramework::SaveGame(name, quick=true, immediate, eSGR_QuickSave(3),
  false, nullptr)` + appends the name to `ArkGame::m_savesThisSession[campaignSlot]` (`this+0x50 +
  slot*0x18`). Slot names (`manual6`, `autosave2`, anything you like) become folders under
  `Saved Games/Arkane Studios/Prey/SaveGames/Campaign<slot>/<name>/` (`save.CSF`, `save.meta`, one
  `<level>.level` per visited level, ~2 MB).
* `CanManualSave()` (0x116CB40, static) gates F5 (`ArkPlayerInput::OnActionQuickSave` 0x15638A0) and the pause
  menu Save; `CanAutoSave()` (0x116CA90) checks `g_blockAutoSave` then calls `CanManualSave()` - a hook on the
  latter must let calls from inside `CanAutoSave` through. A hidden "ironman" option exists
  (`ArkDifficultyComponent::m_difficultyOptions[0]`).
* Loading: `ArkGame::LoadLastSave(listener)` (0x116EB30) -> `IGameFramework::LoadGame(name, quick=true,
  ignoreDelay=false)` (`+0x2A0`); return `eLGR_NoSavesExist` (7) from a hook to refuse quietly. F9 =
  `ArkPlayerInput::OnActionLoadLastSave` (0x1563460); pause menu screens =
  `ArkPauseMenu::OpenSaveLoadMenu(bool bSave)` (0x1370300). **Issue loads only from `UpdateBeforeSystem`**:
  `LoadGame` runs synchronously and tearing the level down from the post-`CSystem::Update` hook crashed the
  Chairloader GUI (null `ImGui::GetIO()`).
* **Load completion**: the player entity *survives* a same-level save load, so "player gone and back" misses
  it. `ArkGame::PostSerialize()` (0x116FAE0) runs once at the end of every save load - hook it.
  `ArkGame::OnSaveGame()` (0x116F4B0) runs after any save. `ArkGame::m_saveFileToLoad` (string @ `+0xD0`)
  holds a pending load.
* Play clock: `ArkGame::m_campaignPlayTime` (uint64 ms @ `+0xE8`, +1000 per accumulated second via
  `m_campaignTimerAccumulator` float @ `+0xF0`) counts active play only and is serialized in saves.
* Campaign slot: `IGameFramework` `+0x1D8` GetArkSaveLoadSystem -> `+0x08` GetCampaignSlot.

## 11. Where the data lives (for XML-side changes)

`ChairManager/PreyFiles/` (Chairloader's extraction of the paks): `Ark/` (game data: `Dialog/VoiceLibrary.xml`,
`Dialog/BinkSubtitles/`, `VisualEffects/ArkPostEffects.xml` + `ArkPostEffectParams.xml`,
`Campaign/POILibrary.xml`, ...), `Libs/GameAudio/` (ATL controls, preloads), `Localization/English_xml/`
(`voices/Voice_*.xml`, UI strings), `Levels/`. `GameSDK/Videos/` for Binks. Options the menu writes are cvars
(`gameOptions.xml`, e.g. `hud_reticleSetting`).

## 12. Quick checklist when something "does nothing" or crashes

* A smoothed value that snaps or freezes while the code is right -> the *step* is garbage -> a callee wrote past
  a stack struct (trap 4). Look for structs the game fills in.
* A hook that seems to run but the game ignores the result -> check the SDK vtable slot against a decompiled
  caller (section 3) or the struct-return convention (traps 1/2).
* Crash with a small absolute address (0xC, 0x10) right after a call into the game -> an undeclared out
  parameter (trap 5).
* Crash in `vsprintf` under Chairloader's aux geom -> `Draw2dLabel` (trap 6).
* Audio "plays" but is silent -> not loaded (dialog manager) or executed on the unpositioned global object.
* A per-frame value read from `ITimer::GetFrameTime()` is 0 in menus/pause; use real time for effects.
* Text/quads in the wrong place -> `eDrawText_800x600` / `Draw2dImage` virtual space vs. pixels.

Questions, corrections or requests for specific decompiles: open an issue on any of the three repositories.
